subject.title: claude-cli backend: no pre-compaction handoff flush + scary bare 100% context display

question: Should native CLI backends expose an OpenClaw pre-transition handoff contract, and which backend state is authoritative enough to drive user-visible context stages?
rationale: Current main intentionally delegates compaction to native harnesses, but no existing contract defines safe flush execution, subscription-auth behavior, exact transition timing, or authoritative stage reporting.

options.title: Add lifecycle contract
options.body: Define a generic backend pre-transition hook and context-state events, then implement Claude CLI and usage/status rendering against that contract.

options.title: Clarify status only
options.body: Suppress or label the CLI context meter now while leaving durable handoff entirely to the native harness.

options.title: Keep current boundary
options.body: Continue documenting that CLI backends own compaction and provide no OpenClaw handoff guarantee.

recommendation.title: Add lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Define a generic backend pre-transition hook and context-state events, then implement Claude CLI and usage/status rendering against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work established the native-compaction ownership contract that this decision would extend.
